answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging each identity a non-transferable history: an agent must complete audited work before gaining access to valuable jobs, much as a ship must clear inspection at a wharf before loading cargo. Trust then works like an opal, its worth lying in a unique accumulated record that cannot be copied by minting a new name. A single pigment, a cryptographic link between past performance, locked stake, and penalties, means misbehavior stains that history, so cloning identities requires paying the cost of building each reputation again.
